steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: Atlas maps show large areas (continents, countries, regions) at small scales. They display general patterns such as climate zones, population density, biomes, and political boundaries. | Exam Tip: When describing patterns on atlas maps, always use the language of distribution: "concentrated in...", "sparse in...", "follows the coastline...", "clusters around...", "increases from north to south..." Always use named places and compass directions. | Key Fact: Ordnance Survey (OS) maps are the standard mapping used in GCSE Geography exams. The most common scales are 1:50,000 (Landranger - covers a larger area, less detail) and 1:25,000 (Explorer - covers a smaller area, more detail). | Rule: "Along the corridor, then up the stairs" - always read the easting (horizontal number along
